A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ATRI and its KCL/CACL strategies. The complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original retrieval, consistency, and training-cost measurements in Tables 1–4, plus embedding visualizations and retrieval case results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains those empirical results and adds translation-quality measurements, LaBSE encoder experiments, and failed-case retrieval rankings.

M1.justification: KCL's simultaneous multilingual training and CACL's audio-English-random-language alignment retain the same procedures and losses. LaBSE is an additional experimental encoder configuration; Appendix E's squared-distance objective supports the alignment analysis rather than replacing the training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate bidirectional retrieval on AudioCaps and Clotho in the same eight languages. The LaBSE experiment uses AudioCaps, and the translation audit examines existing test captions. The xsim/xsim++ discussion concerns prior encoder performance, not newly evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: ML-CLAP remains the evaluated comparator against CACL and KCL. The supplementary LaBSE experiment uses this same comparator set with a common encoder configuration. Newly discussed related methods are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The original fine-tuning settings and retrieval metrics remain unchanged. v3 adds an AudioCaps-only LaBSE configuration under the same stated settings and a test-set audit using back-translation followed by embedding cosine similarity. These are additional evaluation protocols, not revisions to the main experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix A examines translated-caption fidelity, Appendix B tests dependence on the text encoder, and Appendix D adds two failed retrieval cases alongside the retained successful cases. Together these substantially expand diagnostic analysis beyond v1's embedding visualizations and successful examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added language averages and similarity measurements are point estimates, not new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the original case rankings are unchanged. New results include translation similarities of 90.3–95.6, LaBSE retrieval scores and MRV values of 14.73/11.13/9.46 for ML-CLAP/CACL/KCL, and failed-case rankings. These are substantial supplementary result sets. Table 6 ambiguously labels both baseline rows as ML-CLAP (eng).

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives the arithmetic mean of language embeddings as the minimizer of summed squared distances; v1 only states the mean-alignment intuition. The existing SGD weight-error and Adam momentum arguments are retained in Appendix F, with notation and typesetting corrections.

C1.justification: Both versions attribute multilingual retrieval inconsistency to training-data distribution error, propose KCL and CACL for different performance/resource priorities, and claim improved recall and consistency. The revised abstract and added supporting evidence preserve these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets high back-translation similarity as indicating limited hallucination and attributes failed retrieval cases to semantically overlapping captions. These extend the interpretation of reliability and failure conditions. Existing explanations involving dataset noise, language differences, and the SGD/Adam limitation remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies DeepSeek V3 for back-translation, RoBERTa-large for similarity assessment, and LaBSE for the supplementary encoder experiment, which inherits the stated setup. Main hyperparameters, hardware information, and the code-availability promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of Wu et al. (2023), Silva et al. (2023), and Ghosh et al. (2023, 2025), while removing the Mei et al. (2022) triplet-loss discussion. Feng et al. (2020) is added for LaBSE. Positioning against multilingual ML-CLAP remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract, expands related-work prose and case discussion, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements and appendix cross-references. The main section sequence and most methodological and experimental prose are retained, so this is a focused editorial revision.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the diagnostic displays with Tables 5–8 and 10 and a new failure-case Figure 6. It recaptions Figure 5, regroups the retained embedding plots, and relocates the original case table as Table 9. The main table formats and two-column layout remain stable.

improvement.justification: The LaBSE experiment provides evidence beyond the previously sole encoder, while translation auditing and failed cases strengthen scrutiny of data quality and failure behavior. The alignment derivation also clarifies the rationale. These gains are limited by the audit's indirect nature and new reporting errors, including Table 6's duplicate baseline label and Appendix D's reversed success/failure figure references.
